segments.text: Episode twenty-one. Next stop... dark energy.
Since the Big Bang, the universe has been expanding. Galaxies are moving away from each other.
segments.headline: The universe is expanding

segments.text: In nineteen ninety-eight, astronomers studying exploding stars found something shocking. The expansion is speeding up.
segments.headline: 1998: it's speeding up

segments.text: The discovery won the Nobel Prize in Physics in twenty eleven.
Whatever is causing it, we call dark energy. It makes up about sixty-eight percent of the universe.

visual.label: of the universe is dark energy

segments.text: And new measurements hint that dark energy might be changing over time. Nobody knows what it really is.
segments.headline: The biggest mystery in physics

segments.text: Tomorrow, we look at the oldest light in the universe. Next stop: the afterglow of the Big Bang. Follow, so you don't miss episode twenty-two.
